summary: 音乐影响情绪，也能在静听时激活与运动相关的脑区。研究者把大调、小调的情感差异与日常声音线索相联系，并借愉悦和节奏实验探究听觉与身体反应之间的关系。
logic: 作曲经验提出情绪问题
从声音语调和奖赏寻找解释
听觉运动联系的研究前景

paragraphs.brief: 推荐算法引出的音乐偏好之谜
sentences: Robert Matthews looks at research into the effects of music.
罗伯特·马修斯研究音乐的影响。
Music is becoming ever more popular electronically.
以电子方式收听音乐越来越受欢迎。
To meet our craving for music, internet sites are using increasingly sophisticated ways of putting us in touch with artists we may not even know we like.
为满足人们对音乐的需求，网站正用越来越精细的方法推荐一些我们自己都不知道会喜欢的艺人。
Most work by trawling our existing files or online listening habits and looking for patterns so they can recommend new artists for their subscribers to listen to.
多数网站会检索我们的音乐文件或网上收听记录，从中找出规律，再向订阅者推荐新的艺人。
The search often turns up surprises.
搜寻结果往往出人意料
But is it possible to tease apart our likes and dislikes to identify precisely what it is about some music that thrills us or leaves us cold?
可我们能否拆解这些喜好，准确找出音乐中哪些因素能让我们兴奋，哪些又让我们无动于衷？
paragraphs.gist: 网络音乐平台能从听众的收藏和收听记录推荐陌生艺人，有时甚至出乎本人意料，由此引出一个问题，究竟哪些声音会打动我们？

paragraphs.brief: 音乐感染力为何迟入研究视野
sentences: For centuries composers have sought to create unforgettable music using accepted notions about the emotional appeal of certain combinations of sounds, yet only now are scientists starting to uncover what it is about these combinations that can have such a dramatic effect on our minds.
几个世纪以来，作曲家一直试图利用某些声音组合的情感吸引力的公认概念来创造难以忘怀的音乐，然而，现在科学家们才开始发现这些组合对我们的思维产生如此巨大影响。
Given that archaeologists have found musical instruments played by Neanderthals at least 50,000 years ago, why have scientists taken so long to investigate such a source of pleasure?
考古学家已找到尼安德特人至少五万年前演奏的乐器，那么科学家为什么过了这么久才研究这种乐趣？
paragraphs.gist: 作曲家早已懂得利用声音组合唤起情绪，连尼安德特人也留下了乐器，但科学家直到近年才开始追究音乐为何具有这种影响。

paragraphs.brief: 研究音乐情绪的两道障碍
sentences: ‘For psychologists, who are always desperate to show that their work is rigorous, there’s an image problem in tackling the emotionality of music,’ says Professor Norman Cook of Kansai University in Osaka, Japan, one of the pioneers of the new science of music.
日本大阪关西大学的诺曼·库克教授是音乐心理研究的先行者之一。他说：“心理学家总想证明自己的研究足够严谨，研究音乐如何影响情绪，在学术形象上有一道难关。”
‘Emotion is such a slippery topic.’
“情绪是个很难界定的研究对象。”

The other problem, says Cook, is the long-standing principle among psychologists that our response to music is an acquired one, rather than something that is stimulated by the effect of sound on our brain cells.
库克说，另一重障碍是心理学界长期认为，人对音乐的反应源于后天习得，而非声音刺激脑细胞的直接结果。
Yet one of the first insights to emerge from this new branch of psychology is that music affects our brains at a very basic level.
然而，从这个新的心理学分支中最先产生的洞察力之一在于音乐影响我们的大脑在非常基本的层次上。
paragraphs.gist: 情绪难以测量，心理学界又曾把音乐反应视为后天习得，因此相关研究起步很晚，新发现则显示音乐能直接作用于大脑的基础机制。

sentences: Together with his colleague, Professor Takefumi Hayashi, Cook has been investigating one of the best-known examples of the emotional impact of music: the difference between major and minor chords.
库克和同事林武美教授一直在研究一个典型例子，即大和弦与小和弦带来的不同情绪。
For centuries, composers have known that notes arranged to form major chords sound happy and upbeat, while those in minor chords sound mournful.
数百年来，作曲家都知道，音符组成大和弦时听来欢快昂扬，组成小和弦时则显得哀伤。
In tests, even three-year-olds have been shown to link music in a major mode to happy faces and minor modes to sad faces.
测试表明，就连三岁儿童也会把大调音乐与愉快的面孔、小调音乐与悲伤的面孔联系起来。
paragraphs.gist: 大和弦听来明快，小和弦听来忧伤，库克等人的测试发现，连三岁儿童也会把大调和小调分别与笑脸和悲伤表情相配。

paragraphs.brief: 音高变化传达的情绪信号
sentences: According to Cook, analysis of how people respond to notes suggests a link with how our brains interpret certain sounds in everyday life.
库克认为，人们对音符的反应，可能与大脑解读日常声音的方式有关。
He points out that sad-sounding minor chords can be formed by raising the pitch of any of a set of notes, while dropping the pitch produces a major chord.
他指出，把一组音符中的某个音升高，可以形成听起来忧伤的小和弦，降低音高则能产生大和弦。

The same change in pitch works as an emotional telltale in communication between some mammals, where rising pitch is used to communicate weakness or defeat, while falling pitch signals social dominance.
在一些哺乳动物的交流中，音高变化也能透露情绪，声调上升表示示弱或认输，声调下降则表示占据支配地位。
It’s also present in our speech.
我们说话时也有这种现象。
‘A rising inflection is used to denote questions, politeness or deference, whereas a falling inflection signals dominance,’ says Cook.
库克说：“上扬的语调可以表达疑问、礼貌或恭敬，下降的语调则传递支配意味。”
paragraphs.gist: 库克把和弦的情绪色彩与日常交流相联系，某些哺乳动物和人类都以上扬、下降的音高分别传递示弱或支配等信号。

paragraphs.brief: 悦耳音乐激活古老奖赏回路
sentences: This suggests that music in major and minor modes taps into some very basic features of how we relate to the world and each other – perhaps dating back millions of years.
这表明大小调音乐触及人类与外界和彼此相处的一些基本方式，这些机制也许可以追溯到几百万年前。
Could music in general be doing something similar?
音乐一般会做类似的事情吗？
Quite possibly, according to research into how music triggers certain types of brain activity.
关于音乐如何触发特定脑部活动的研究表明，很有这种可能。
At McGill University in Canada, Professor Robert Zatorre and his colleagues have carried out studies in which volunteers listen to different types of music while their brain activity is monitored.
在加拿大麦吉尔大学，Robert Zatorre教授及其同事开展了一些研究，让志愿者在监测他们的大脑活动时聆听不同类型的音乐。
The biggest surprise was the evidence that pleasurable music activates brain circuitry which has been in existence in the human brain for thousands of years, says Zatorre.
萨托雷说，最出乎意料的是，令人愉悦的音乐能够激活在人类大脑中已存在数千年的神经回路。
‘We share it with rats and other distant relatives on the evolutionary tree – and it’s typically associated with biological rewards, like food, for example.’
“我们与大鼠等进化上的远亲都拥有这套回路，它通常与食物等生物性奖赏有关。”
paragraphs.gist: 麦吉尔大学监测志愿者听音乐时的大脑活动，发现悦耳的音乐会激活古老的奖赏回路，这套回路也响应食物等生物性奖赏。

paragraphs.brief: 聆听节奏也会调动运动脑区
sentences: At the University of Oxford, Dr Joyce Chen has been looking into another celebrated feature of music – the irresistibility of rhythm.
牛津大学的乔伊丝·陈博士研究的是音乐的另一种特性，即节奏让人难以抗拒的吸引力。
Her interest was sparked by studies involving patients with movement difficulties.
她的兴趣来自对行动有困难的病人的研究。
If music that had a strong rhythm – say, a marching band – was played to these patients, they were able to improve their walking ability, says Chen.
陈说，给这些患者播放节奏鲜明的音乐，例如军乐队的进行曲，他们的行走能力就会改善。

In an attempt to find out why the simple act of listening to music might help disabled patients, Dr Chen and colleagues from the International Laboratory for Brain, Music and Sound Research in Montreal carried out brain scans on volunteers who were listening to rhythmic sounds.
为弄清仅仅听音乐为何就能帮助行动不便的人，陈博士和蒙特利尔国际大脑、音乐与声音研究实验室的同事对收听节奏声的志愿者进行了脑扫描。
The criteria for selecting these volunteers were that they should be in first-rate physical health but musically untrained.
入选的志愿者身体十分健康，但没有接受过音乐训练。
The results have been another revelation.
结果又是一个启示。

Chen and her colleagues found the rhythms triggered activity in parts of the brain linked to hearing, but something even more surprising was that the rhythms also triggered activity in the motor regions of the brain, linked to active movement.
团队发现，节奏会激活听觉相关区域，更令人意外的是，负责身体动作的运动区也活跃起来。
paragraphs.gist: 强烈的节奏能帮助行动困难者走得更好，而对健康且未受音乐训练者的脑扫描显示，光听节奏就会同时调动听觉区和运动区。

paragraphs.brief: 听觉与动作的临床联系
sentences: ‘Somehow, the mere act of just listening triggers motor-neural activity.
“单是听，就能以某种方式激发运动神经活动。”
Maybe this is one reason why we often tap our feet, move or dance when hearing music,’ says Chen.
陈说：“我们听到音乐常会用脚打拍子、随节奏摆动或起舞，这可能是原因之一。”

She believes the discovery of this deep connection between music and movement may cast light on why disabled patients can benefit from listening to music – and could also prove useful with other impairments such as those involved in sound production.
她认为，音乐与运动的深层联系也许能解释为何听音乐有益于行动不便者，也可能为其他障碍，例如发声障碍，提供线索。
‘It’s been shown that people who talk with a stutter might have problems in this auditory-motor loop.’
“研究已发现，口吃者的听觉—运动回路可能存在问题。”
paragraphs.gist: 听音乐就会激发运动神经活动，这可能解释人为何随节拍拍脚或起舞，也给步行困难和口吃等障碍的研究提供了线索。

paragraphs.brief: 音乐辨别能力的差异与训练
sentences: For researchers working in this new area of science, these early discoveries hold the promise of much more to come.
对于在这个新的科学领域工作的研究人员来说，这些早期发现有望带来更多的成就。
Zatorre and his colleagues are investigating whether some people have more musical brains than others.
萨托雷及同事正在研究有些人的大脑是否天生更擅长处理音乐。
‘We can see certain subtle brain features that can tell us how well somebody can do things like identify a slight change in a melody,’ explains Zatorre.
萨托雷解释说：“我们能观察到一些细微的脑部特征，从而判断一个人能多好地辨认出旋律中的微小变化。”
‘This ability could be enhanced by training – just like someone born with a predisposition to building strong muscles can enhance them by taking up weightlifting.’
“这种能力可以通过训练提高，就像天生容易长肌肉的人也能通过举重变得更强壮。”
paragraphs.gist: 萨托雷用细微的脑部特征预测人辨别旋律变化的能力，并认为先天差异并不妨碍这种能力通过训练进一步提高。

items.en: a reference to studies involving children
items.why: 题干问“reference to studies involving children (涉及儿童的研究)”。只有 D 段明确提到对“三岁儿童” 的测试，因此 14 选 D。

items.en: a mention of the discovery of significant artefacts
items.why: 题干里的“discovery of significant artefacts (重要文物的发现)”对应考古学家发现的尼安德特人乐器，这是典型的“artefacts”,所以选 B。

items.en: reasons why a particular aspect of music has not been researched
items.zh: 为何没有研究音乐的一个特定方面
items.why: 心理学界长期把对音乐的反应视作后天习得，也担心研究音乐情绪缺乏严谨形象；两点都阻碍了研究。

items.en: a mention of an unexpected discovery involving two different areas of the brain
items.zh: 提到一个意外发现涉及到大脑的两个不同区域
items.why: 这里先说听觉区被激活，再说“更令人吃惊的是” 运动区也被激活，正好是“涉及大脑两个不同区域的意外发现”,所以 17 选 G。

items.en: a comparison of tone variations produced by certain animals and humans
items.zh: 对某些动物和人类产生的音调变化的比较
items.why: 该句把哺乳动物的音高变化和人类说话中的升降调放在一起比较，正是“a comparison of tone variations produced by certain animals and humans”,因此 18 选 E。

items.en: The participants in this study led by Dr Chen were chosen because they were not musicians, and they demonstrated a good state of ________.
items.zh: 陈博士主持的这项研究选择参与者时，要求他们既不是音乐家，又具有良好的________状况。
items.why: 空格前有“a good state of…”,需要一个健康状态的名词短语。原文是“first-rate physical health”,符合“good state of physical health”。不超过两词，因此答案写 physical health。

items.en: The participants were given ________ while music with a very noticeable rhythm was being played.
items.zh: 在播放节奏十分鲜明的音乐时，研究人员给参与者做了________。
items.why: 这里描述合作研究的具体做法: 在听节奏音乐时对志愿者做“brain scans”,与摘要中“were given 20…while music…was being played” 完全对应，所以 20 3% brain scans。

items.en: Previous research had indicated that listening to this type of music seemed to be of assistance to some ________ people.
items.zh: 以往研究表明，这类音乐似乎能帮助一些________人士。
items.why: 摘要中的“this type of music”指前文所说强节奏音乐。相关旧研究提到这种音乐帮助的是“patients with movement difficulties / disabled patients”。空后已有单词“people”,因此只需填一个形容词 disabled,构成“disabled people”,与文中“disabled patients” 意义相同，且用词来自原文。

items.en: By listening to it, their ________ ability had definitely got better.
items.zh: 聆听这种音乐后，他们的________能力确实有所改善。
items.why: 回到对应内容“陈说，给这些患者播放节奏鲜明的音乐，例如军乐队的进行曲，他们的行走能力就会改善。”，再按题干要求写出答案。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空最多填两个词。

items.en: Research into the brain activity set off by music may help people with speech defects.
items.zh: 研究音乐引起的脑活动，可能对言语障碍者有所帮助。

items.en: It may be possible in time to improve a person’s ability to recognise certain musical characteristics.
items.zh: 人辨认某些音乐特征的能力，或许能随时间推移而逐渐提高。

items.en: The way listeners react to certain musical combinations may be similar to the way they react to other noises.
items.zh: 人对某些音符组合的反应，可能与对其他声音的反应相似。

items.en: When a person reacts positively to music, the same parts of the brain are stimulated as when certain animals react to a positive outcome.
items.zh: 人听音乐感到愉悦时受到刺激的脑区，与某些动物获得奖赏时受到刺激的脑区相同。

points: 题干问“reference to studies involving children (涉及儿童的研究)”。只有 D 段明确提到对“三岁儿童” 的测试，因此 14 选 D。
回到对应内容“陈说，给这些患者播放节奏鲜明的音乐，例如军乐队的进行曲，他们的行走能力就会改善。”，再按题干要求写出答案。
clauses: For centuries, composers have known … sound happy and upbeat, while those in minor chords sound mournful.
“that notes arranged to form major chords”补足 known 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 known 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
At McGill University in Canada, Professor Robert Zatorre and his colleagues have carried out studies ….
“in which volunteers listen to different types of music while their brain activity is monitored”修饰前面的 studies。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 which 时，回看 studies，再把修饰信息接回主句。
